_README: Integration calls the endpoint catalog cannot serve, as they stood when
tests/unit/test_integration_call_contract.py was written (2026-08-30).
This is a RATCHET, not an exemption list. It is asserted exactly in both
directions: a NEW breach fails CI, and so does a STALE entry, so fixing
one means deleting its line. Adding a line is a decision to ship a test
that cannot fail -- against a live Ghidra every one of these still
returns 200, because AnnotationScanner simply does not find an
undeclared parameter and uses the default instead.
The read-only suite is deliberately absent: its ten breaches were fixed
in the same change, and test_baseline_carries_no_readonly_entries stops
one being re-admitted here.
Three shapes appear, all mechanical to fix:
unknown_parameter   The name is wrong, or the endpoint has no such
parameter at all. /list_functions is the common
one: ListingService documents it as 'List all
functions (no pagination)' and declares only
`program`, so every `limit` sent to it is dropped.
Pagination lives on /list_functions_enhanced and
/search_functions.
method_not_allowed  A POST endpoint called with GET. A live server
answers 404, and these tests were written to
accept it. Note that several are POSTs because
they WRITE -- correcting the call also moves the
test into a mutating tier, which is a judgement
call per test, not a search-and-replace.
no_such_endpoint    The route does not exist. PR #459 settled that the
@McpTool annotations are authoritative, so this is
a broken test, not a missing feature. Known
replacements: /batch_rename_variables ->
/rename_variables; /run_script ->
/run_ghidra_script or /run_script_inline. The
surviving hash surface is /get_function_hash and
/get_bulk_function_hashes; neither a persistent
index nor a reverse hash->function lookup exists,
so /build_function_hash_index and
/lookup_function_by_hash describe a capability
this server does not have.
